column1: # Graded SPEC cases for harness/test-recall-runner.sh part 15 (bead
# WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE FILE FROM CASES.tsv rather than more rows in it.
# Parts 1 and 2 loop over every CASES row, and part 2 corroborates each code
# by building a VALUE scaffold itself -- `ASSUME Answer = Canonical` with an
# empty .cfg -- and running harness/verdict.sh over it. A spec rep has no
# value and no such scaffold, so a SPEC row in that file would have been
# corroborated against a module that means nothing. Part 15 does the same
# corroboration in the shape a spec rep actually has: it fills the scaffold,
# runs verdict.sh over the pair, and compares the per-scaffold code.
# One row per answer submitted against a SPEC row in REPS.tsv beside this
# file. Tab-delimited, literal first field CASE. Seven fields, in order:
#   1  marker    the literal CASE
#   2  id        stable
#   3  rep       a SPEC id in REPS.tsv
#   4  grade     correct | incorrect | construct-missing | parse-error | other
#   5  rc        the code recall/recall.sh exits with on this answer
#   6  answer    the TLA+ submitted
#   7  vector    comma-separated, the code EACH scaffold returns, in the
#                scaffolds' own order
# FIELDS 5 AND 7 ARE DIFFERENT NUMBERS AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT. Field
# 7 is what TLC said, one code per machine. Field 5 is what the runner exits
# with, and on a wrong answer it is 5 -- the runner's own code for a vector
# that did not match -- rather than any code in field 7. A suite that pinned
# only field 5 would pass over a runner that stopped running the scaffolds at
# all, and one that pinned only field 7 would pass over a runner that ran them
# and then reported the wrong grade.
# EVERY NUMBER IN BOTH FIELDS WAS MEASURED on TLC2 2026.07.31.184830 on
# 2026-10-17: field 5 through recall/recall.sh and field 7 through
# harness/verdict.sh over an independently filled scaffold.
# WHAT EACH ROW IS FOR:
#   D001        the canonical, one scaffold, rc 0
#   D002        a STRONGER correct form. Its vector is 0, so the value side
#               was accepted and field 7 of the rep -- `\bWF_` -- is the only
#               thing that turned it away. A K095 rep asks for the WEAKER of
#               the two promises, so strong fairness is not an alternate
#               spelling of it
#   D003, D004  wrong answers. One names the wrong subaction, one promises
#               nothing
#   D005        THE TRAP THE CONSTRUCT GATE EXISTS FOR, and it is the reason
#               every shipped SPEC row carries a field 7. `<>(n = 2)` is the
#               goal asserted as a hypothesis rather than a fairness
#               condition, its vector is 0, and no exit code can tell. Only
#               field 7 can
#   D006        a code outside the gradeable set. Fairness over the initial
#               predicate rather than over an action is 255, and the runner
#               reports that rather than calling the answer wrong
#   D007        the canonical of a BATTERY: it has to hold on fix-near and
#               fail on fix-far, so the key is 0,13
#   D008, D009  the two reasons a battery exists. Both are too weak, both
#               hold on BOTH machines, and a single run against fix-near
#               alone would have passed either one
#   D010, D011  the action hole's canonical and the UNCHANGED spelling of it.
#               Both reach the same state graph, so both are 0
#   D012        the swapped variable, caught by the scaffold's INVARIANT at
#               12 rather than by the fingerprint, which is identical
#   D013        a wrong step shape, caught by the fingerprint at 10. A false
#               POSTCONDITION is rc 10
#   D014        a parse error, which is its own report rather than a wrong
#               answer
